sentences.text: Gettyia is an extinct genus of enantiornithean bird, a clade of early avialans, known only from the single species G. gloriae.
This animal is known from a single fossilized right tarsometatarsus bone, which is similar to those of other North American avisaurids but much smaller in size.
The skeleton possessed a knob-like structure on the front edge of its second metatarsal and featured extensively fused third and fourth metatarsals near the ankle and toes.
The specific name gloriae honors Gloria Siebrecht, a volunteer fossil collector who discovered the original specimen.
The unique position of the tibialis cranialis tubercule suggests that Gettyia had a more specialized lifestyle than other avisaurids.
The species was originally described as Avisaurus gloriae in 1995 based on a single tarsometatarsus fossil found in Glacier County, Montana.
The genus Gettyia was later established by Atterholt and colleagues in 2018.

Gettyia is an extinct genus of enantiornithean bird belonging to the family Avisauridae, which serves as its parent group.
Fossils of Gettyia date to the late Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous period, living between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago.
Gettyia inhabited both humid low-lying swamps near the Western Interior Seaway and the drier uplands leading to the Rocky Mountains.
